A poor scanned PDF (image-only, no embedded text layer) [NL-021#NL-021-S02] stalls the enterprise deployment at ingestion because the KnowledgeHub's current pipeline relies on standard PDF text extraction; the standard parser fails to detect a text layer in image-only documents, resulting in empty indexes or failure to extract the text [NL-029#NL-029-S05][NL-031#NL-031-S04]. This leads to incomplete text extraction and low-quality or missing answers [NL-010#NL-010-S06]. Critically, because there is no text layer, the system cannot index the text or generate citation anchors [NL-018#NL-018-S05].

The downstream impact on TutorChat is that it either returns answers with no source citations (because it cannot find text offsets) or generates citations that point to the entire document (e.g., page 1 of a 250-page PDF) instead of a specific section [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. This can also cause TutorChat to omit critical content entirely, as in the case where it missed two critical alarm threshold steps from a scanned ventilator protocol [NL-018#NL-018-S05].

This directly prevents go-live because incomplete citations fail the go-live validation threshold, which requires 85% citation correctness [NL-031#NL-031-S04]. The failure blocks compliance sign-off: BrightPath Healthcare's compliance officers refuse to sign off on a general rollout, restricting the deployment to their initial 100-user group rather than the full 6,500 employees [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. In practice, this drags out onboarding—Northstar Financial's pilot kickoff was delayed by three weeks [NL-010#NL-010-S06], and BrightPath experienced a 9.5-week onboarding due to manual formatting checks on scanned compliance files [NL-031#NL-031-S04]—until an automated OCR pipeline (planned for August 2026) can handle the extraction and allow for validation reviews [NL-018#NL-018-S05].
